input.quote: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
input.rationale: Section 14.3 selects New York substantive law, which is our preferred governing law, but the Agreement contains no venue, forum, or dispute-resolution provision anywhere (no arbitration clause either — searches for jurisdiction, venue, court and dispute return only unrelated indemnity/severability references). Without an exclusive forum, IBM could sue us in any competent court, so the clause fails the venue half of both the preferred and fallback positions. We added a single sentence fixing exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, with a customary carve-out for temporary injunctive relief, leaving the governing-law sentence untouched.

ops.text: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York will have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or related to this Agreement, provided that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement chooses New York law but names no forum, so we added exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, with only temporary injunctive relief available elsewhere.
proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County forum to the Choice of Law clause
